title: Lattice Grid
tagline: A fixed lattice of nodes and connectors whose content re-rolls on the beat, lit by a moving field.
method: A lattice is generated once and never moves. Each site carries a glyph — empty, dot, ring or pad — and each adjacency may be lit as a connector; boxes are closed rings of connectors around one cell. That content re-rolls on the musical beat, only partly, so state at beat b depends on beat b-1. A smooth illumination field sweeps across gating which elements appear and how hot they are; a second, faster field assigns hue. Everything composites ADDITIVELY into a padded float buffer and blooms, so dense clusters run to white on their own. The swappable part is the lattice: two geometries differ by one class attribute.

output.note: World units are the 1080x1920 reference frame and `RenderConfig.scale` maps to output px. The lattice is generated to whatever `nx`/`ny` you give it at whatever pitch — a landscape frame is a different `RenderConfig`, not different code. Note the atlas must be baked PER OUTPUT SCALE (`atlas_for(cfg)`); this is the one place the format has bitten hard.

modules.what: The swappable part. `Lattice` base with CSR adjacency, site-pair to edge-id lookup and closed-loop boxes; `SquareLattice` (8-neighbour), `HexLattice` (`honeycomb` = hexagon cells at 3-neighbour, `triangular` = hex-packed at 6-neighbour), and `build()`.
Pre-baked anti-aliased alpha stamps at 4x4 sub-pixel phases: dot, ring, pad, and one per link direction-and-length.
The beat-epoch timeline: glyph per site, lit edges, momentum-biased walks (PCB traces), boxes, endcaps, and the three-group crossfade.

`Illumination` (clustered plane waves, wandering spiral arms, drifting flares, fractal octaves, with an ambient floor and a hot overdrive), `Twinkle` (independent per-element flicker), `Palette` (CDF-flattened noise into a bimodal LUT), `envelope` (the tempo arc).
`Frame`: padded additive float32 buffer, `splat` with a buffered fast path for nodes and scatter-add for links, a decimated halo chain, an anamorphic streak, exposure tonemap, and frame-seeded grain.
`ChannelDelay` — a ring buffer that turns a stream of MONO frames into RGB by delaying the channels against each other. This is where the colour actually comes from.
The glitch LAYER: block displacement, copy, solid-lit blocks, row tears, drips. Applied to the mono frame BEFORE the delay.
The circuits: chains of up to ten nodes plus short branches, about 26% of sites, each chain lighting on ONE shared schedule.

A drawable eye that returns three fields — `lit`, `conn` (how wired-up) and `layer` (depth). Almond lids from two different curves, a foreshortening iris, an offset pupil, fibres, a limbal ring, specular, saccades and blinks.
Holofoil: a thin-film spectral LUT, band cycles, warp, depth-driven hue shift, specular sheen.
`transmission` (a cached distance transform of the rasterised seams) and `SourceGrid` (a coarse under-surface field with a cascading upsample).
`dry_report` / `render_stills` / `render_scene`, ffmpeg pipe, atomic output, and the RGB-delay pre-roll.
`RenderConfig`, `SOURCE_PITCH`, NVENC probe, ffmpeg resolution. Unlike the rest of this repository the rate defaults here are deliberately HIGH — see the parameters table.
Substrate invariants: coordination number, link-stamp lengths against real edge lengths, and that a box is a closed ring.

objects.intro: Adding a geometry means a `Lattice` subclass providing `sites`, `edges`, `edge_kind`, `link_specs` and `sample_box`. Nothing downstream changes. Measured at the reference pitch on a 1080x1920 frame.

items.name: SquareLattice
items.what: Square cells, 8-neighbour. Links at 0/45/90/135 deg. ~5,858 sites, ~22,957 edges.
items.notes: The only geometry with long straight runs, so the only one that reaches the reference clip's filament coherence.

items.name: HexLattice (honeycomb)
items.what: Hexagon cells, 3-neighbour. Links at 30/90/150 deg. ~5,252 sites, ~7,771 edges.
items.notes: A honeycomb has NO straight runs — every second edge turns 60 deg — so its traces zigzag. That is inherent to the geometry, not a bug. The right density invariant across geometries is lit edges PER NODE, not lit-edge fraction: 38% of honeycomb edges is past percolation and the frame reads as continuous chicken-wire.

items.name: HexLattice (triangular)
items.what: Hex-packed nodes, triangular cells, 6-neighbour. Links at 0/60/120 deg. ~7,140 sites, ~21,063 edges.
items.notes: Registered and passes the substrate check, but has had no density pass — its constants are the pre-deep-pass ones.

items.name: glyph stamps
items.what: dot / ring / pad, plus one stamp per link direction-and-length, each baked at 4x4 sub-pixel phases.
items.notes: The pitch is FRACTIONAL on purpose, so sites do not land on integer pixels. Rounding each stamp puts +/-0.5 px of jitter on a 5 px ring and the lattice reads as mush. The phases cost about 180 KiB.

items.name: walks
items.what: Momentum-biased runs of lit edges — the PCB traces.
items.notes: `walk_straight` near 0.93 selects the zigzag that holds a constant net heading, which is the best a honeycomb can do.

items.name: boxes
items.what: Closed rings of connectors around one cell.

items.name: blend
items.what: The beat crossfade, split into THREE DISJOINT groups: unchanged at full, old-only fading out, new-only fading in.
items.notes: Arithmetically identical to 'old at 1-w plus new at w', but it draws about 1.25x elements during a crossfade instead of 2x, AND it guarantees no site is splatted twice in one call — which is the precondition for the disjoint fast path.

items.name: network chains
items.what: Chains of up to ten nodes with short branches. The CHAIN is the unit that lights, not the node.
items.notes: Every node and edge in a chain shares one schedule, so a circuit energises as a whole. Per-element independent flicker reads as noise precisely because nothing is connected to anything. Measured: 211 chains, 26.0% of sites, sizes 1–15.

items.name: Illumination
items.signature: Illumination(drift, spin, octaves, octave_gain, octave_speed, axis_deg, axis_spread, ambient, hot)
items.what: The gate — clustered plane waves plus wandering spiral arms, drifting flares and fractal octaves.
items.notes: Octave SPEED stays low on purpose: octaves exist for spatial detail, and fast octaves generate high-frequency energy that is spatially SMOOTH, which is exactly what a field cannot be if you want independent per-element motion. `axis_spread` controls whether lit regions are isotropic blobs or elongated diagonal streaks.

items.name: Twinkle
items.what: Independent per-element flicker, indexed by ELEMENT rather than by position.
items.notes: The only source of spatially uncorrelated fast motion in the engine — a band-limited field structurally cannot produce it. Under the RGB-delay colour model this is also the dominant control on saturation. Rate capped around 5 Hz: faster than 1/delay and an element completes a whole cycle inside the delay window, so the channels sample unrelated phases.

items.name: Palette
items.what: CDF-flattened noise indexed into a bimodal LUT.
items.notes: Largely superseded — see the colour note in the README. A bell-shaped field indexed into a segmented LUT piles most sites in whichever segment straddles the middle, and the accent segment is never reached at all; push the field through its own CDF first or the LUT's widths mean nothing.

items.name: envelope
items.what: The tempo arc over the clip — build, climax, plateau, fade.

items.name: ChannelDelay
items.what: Turns mono frames into RGB by delaying the channels. Blue undelayed, green ~0.1 s, red ~0.2 s.
items.notes: Delays are held in SECONDS so a 60 fps render matches a 30 fps reference. The buffer must be PRE-ROLLED before frame 0 or the first fifth of a second comes out greyscale and colour visibly switches on.

objects.intro: A second subject on the same substrate. Where the circuit scenes recreate a reference clip, this one uses the engine to DRAW something. Four mechanisms, each answering one direction.

items.name: eye.lit / conn / layer
items.what: Three independent fields — brightness, how wired-up, and depth. Using all three independently is what produces depth on a flat grid.
items.notes: Details that carry the illusion, in rough order of value: the limbal ring; fibres converging on the PUPIL rather than the iris centre (only visible because the pupil is offset, and the thing that stops it reading as a dartboard); the specular fixed to the LIGHT not the gaze; the lid shadow.

items.name: saccades
items.what: The gaze HOLDS, then moves in about 60 ms.
items.notes: A smoothly drifting gaze reads as a floating balloon. The hold-jump-hold rhythm is most of what makes it alive.

items.name: blinks
items.what: Close fast, open slower, both lids converging on one meeting line below centre.
items.notes: Driving the two lids by independent fractions never actually shuts — it leaves a band open at full closure.

items.name: holofoil
items.what: Thin-film spectral colour, not a hue ramp.
items.notes: Three properties separate it from a rainbow and all three are needed: hue cycles SEVERAL times across the frame so you see bands; the spectrum is thin-film weighted (dwelling in magenta/violet/blue/cyan, passing green quickly, with a wide gold shoulder) rather than perceptually uniform; and hue shifts with viewing DEPTH, which is the actual physics and also the cheapest depth cue available. Plus a narrow high-frequency sheen band that spikes near-white — without it the colour reads as coloured plastic rather than metal.

items.name: panel transmission
items.what: A cached distance transform of the rasterised seams — about 1 at the seams and 0.03 mid-face — with a diffuse source composited UNDER it.
items.notes: Elements splat on top, so they sit ON the surface while colour sits UNDER it. Every multi-scale upsample must CASCADE (double and blur repeatedly); expanding a small buffer in one jump paints visible blocks no subsequent blurring removes, and `SourceGrid.expand` doubles its way up so its divisor must be a power of two.

scenes_intro: Eight compositions in two families. The circuit set recreates a reference clip and is checkable against it; the eye set deliberately departs on blacks, palette and density and is not.

scenes.name: circuit_square
scenes.what: Square cells — the reference geometry. 8-neighbour, links at 0/45/90/135.

scenes.name: circuit_hex
scenes.what: The literal read of 'square cells to hexagons' — the cells you see are hexagons. 3-neighbour.

scenes.name: circuit_tri
scenes.what: The other reading — a denser fabric closer to the square version's connectivity, with hexagonal rings as its box glyph.

scenes.name: eye_foil
scenes.what: Baseline: balanced foil, readable panels, mid density.

scenes.name: eye_foil_deep
scenes.what: How far can the SURFACE go? Faces near-opaque, seams tight and hot — maximum 'light from underneath' before the picture turns to lace.

scenes.name: eye_foil_wide
scenes.what: Can COLOUR carry the layering instead of brightness? Half as many, twice as broad foil bands, and a big depth shift so sclera, iris and pupil separate by hue.

scenes.name: eye_foil_dense
scenes.what: Connectivity at its limit — the iris becomes a solid mesh while the sclera stays scattered dots.

scenes.name: eye_foil_sparse
scenes.what: The opposite end — few elements, source-dominant: the picture is mostly the glowing seams, nodes as accents.

parameters_intro: Ordered roughly by how much they move the picture. Several of these are pinned by measurement rather than taste, and the notes say which.

parameters.name: illum_lo
parameters.meaning: How far up the field a site must be to appear at all. The biggest lever by far — raising it thins lit regions into ARMS rather than shrinking them.

parameters.name: twinkle / twinkle_rate
parameters.meaning: Per-element flicker. Under the RGB-delay colour model this is the dominant control on saturation, because saturation IS how much the mono signal changes across the delay window at bright pixels.
parameters.range: 0.30 gives white 0.33 / sat 0.42; 0.80 gives 0.19 / 0.53. Rate capped near 5 Hz. Shares its high-frequency budget with `grain` — change one, re-measure the other.

parameters.name: node_p / edge_p / walks
parameters.range: On a new lattice, re-derive from EDGES PER NODE. Square: 8.2% of 8 = 0.66. Honeycomb wants about 22% of 3.

parameters.name: churn / xfade
parameters.meaning: What fraction of the lattice re-rolls per beat, and how hard the crossfade is.
parameters.range: ~34% churn. Re-rolling everything is a strobe; re-rolling nothing is a static board with a light moving over it. A LONG crossfade moves all three channels together and stays white — keep it snappy (~0.07).

parameters.name: ambient
parameters.range: A high floor plus strong twinkle makes everything busy everywhere and the frame collapses into uniform confetti with no composition. On a honeycomb, where every edge joins up, a floor invisible on a square lattice draws a continuous faint MESH across the darks.

parameters.name: exposure
parameters.range: Keep it LOW and get brightness from COVERAGE. A clipped pixel is white by definition, and white is the one thing a colour-delay look cannot afford. It is also the wrong control for whiteness generally — use `glow_gain`.

parameters.name: glow_sigma / glow_gain / glow2_gain
parameters.meaning: The halo — which is what smears adjacent elements' hues together before anything is measured.
parameters.range: Bloom is the ENEMY of a delay-based colour: a halo averages many elements, so it changes slowly even when the ink under it is switching hard, and slow-changing means white.

parameters.name: hot_gain
parameters.meaning: How far past the gate a crest drives its elements — the white cores.
parameters.range: Keep low (~0.95) for the same reason as exposure.

parameters.name: dark_depth
parameters.meaning: A separate slow field that multiplies everything and reaches TRUE zero, because the illumination gate has a floor by construction and can never take a region fully out.
parameters.range: Must reach 0. A 'depth' that multiplies by (1-d) + d*v leaves a permanent floor at any value below 1.0 — set to 0.62 it meant not one of 64 tiles ever went dark while the parameter looked reasonable.

parameters.name: grain / grain_floor
parameters.meaning: Per-frame noise, spatial and in the darks.
parameters.range: Per-frame noise in a dark region IS low-level blinking. For true black you need `ambient=0`, `grain_floor` low AND `bg` near zero — all three, or you spend an hour re-rendering.

parameters.name: streak_gain
parameters.range: Near-linear in the setting. A streak you can obviously SEE is roughly 4x too strong.

parameters.name: cq / maxrate
parameters.range: Grain is per-frame noise and therefore incompressible, so this format's encode cost is set almost entirely by `grain`. Measured first-generation: cq 19 / 40M destroys half the grain; cq 17 / 70M is on target. Do NOT measure this with a transcode — re-encoding a master flatters low bitrates by nearly 2x.
